question: What is the primary goal of occupational health hazard control?

options.A: To reduce the cost of buying new equipment
options.B: To punish workers who break safety rules
options.C: To treat workers only after an accident occurs
options.D: To prevent injuries and illnesses before they happen

explanation: Hazard control focuses on stopping workplace dangers from causing harm in the first place rather than just dealing with the aftermath. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h1)

question: Why are nurses considered frontline defenders in occupational health?

options.A: They spot workplace dangers and help protect staff and patients
options.B: They write all the labor laws for the country
options.C: They inspect building foundations for structural damage
options.D: They buy and sell safety gear for factories

explanation: Nurses work closely with people in clinical and industrial spaces, putting them in a prime position to notice health risks and advocate for safety. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h1)

question: Which method ranks highest in the hierarchy of hazard controls?
explanation: Elimination is the most effective control because it completely removes the danger from the workplace. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h2)

question: Why is personal protective equipment placed at the very bottom of the control hierarchy?

options.A: It relies on human behavior and fails if the equipment is damaged
options.B: It is always the most expensive option available
options.C: It completely removes the hazard from the environment
options.D: It is the only method that requires worker training

explanation: PPE is considered a last resort because a mistake by the worker or a tear in the gear still leaves them exposed to the danger. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h2)

question: What is an example of hazard substitution in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Handing out safety glasses at the front desk
options.B: Asking staff to work fewer hours each week
options.C: Replacing latex gloves with nitrile gloves
options.D: Ordering workers to hold their breath near dust

explanation: Substitution involves swapping a dangerous item, like latex that causes allergies, for a safer material that does the same job. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h3)

question: A hospital completely bans the use of a toxic chemical sterilizing agent and buys a safe machine instead. Which control strategy is this?
explanation: Removing the toxic chemical completely from the facility means the hazard has been eliminated. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of an engineering control in the workplace?

options.A: To punish staff who fail to follow safety instructions
options.B: To provide extra clothing to shield the skin from harm
options.C: To force workers to change their daily habits and routines
options.D: To place a physical barrier between the worker and the hazard

explanation: Engineering controls use physical changes to the environment or equipment to keep workers safe without needing constant human oversight. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h4)

question: Why are engineering controls generally preferred over personal protective equipment?

options.A: They do not rely on the worker remembering to wear them correctly every day
options.B: They completely eliminate the hazard from the universe
options.C: They are the only legal requirement for hospitals
options.D: They cost nothing to install and maintain over time

explanation: Engineering controls work automatically in the background, reducing human error in safety maintenance. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h4)

question: Which of the following is an example of an administrative control?

options.A: Rotating staff away from high-noise areas to limit exposure time
options.B: Replacing a toxic cleaning fluid with warm water and soap
options.C: Providing heavy leather boots to construction workers
options.D: Installing a heavy glass shield around a loud machine

explanation: Changing work schedules and rotating job duties to limit exposure time are classic administrative controls. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h5)

question: What is a major limitation of administrative controls compared to engineering controls?

options.A: They are completely invisible to workers and inspectors
options.B: They remove hazards completely from the physical workspace
options.C: They rely heavily on human behavior and can be forgotten or ignored
options.D: They cost more money than buying new factory buildings

explanation: Because administrative controls depend on people following rules and schedules, they fail more easily than automated engineering barriers. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h5)

question: Where does personal protective equipment rank in the hierarchy of hazard controls?

options.A: Below administrative controls but above substitution
options.B: At the very bottom as a last resort
options.C: At the very top as the best choice

explanation: PPE is the last line of defense because it does not stop the hazard itself, only protects the individual wearing it if other controls fail. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h6)

question: A nurse is preparing to care for a patient with an airborne infection. What must be done before entering the room to ensure effective PPE use?

options.A: Ask another staff member to hold their breath for them
options.B: Rely on natural room ventilation to clean the air
options.C: Wear any old pair of cloth gloves found in the utility room
options.D: Select the correct respirator mask and check its fit and seal

explanation: Proper PPE selection and fit checking are essential to ensure the equipment actually blocks the airborne hazard. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of occupational health surveillance?

options.A: To punish workers who report feeling sick on the job
options.B: To catch early signs of work-related illness through regular testing
options.C: To calculate the exact salary of every factory worker
options.D: To replace the need for engineering safety barriers

explanation: Surveillance monitors worker health over time so that illnesses can be detected and treated early before causing permanent damage. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h7)

question: Why are regular hearing tests important for workers in noisy industrial plants?

options.A: They detect early hearing loss before the damage becomes permanent
options.B: They make the factory machines run much more quietly
options.C: They prove that loud noise has no effect on human ears
options.D: They replace the need for wearing earplugs

explanation: Routine testing spots subtle hearing changes early, prompting better protection before deafness occurs. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h7)

question: Which setting is a community health nurse most likely to visit when addressing occupational hazards?

options.A: Local small businesses and agricultural farms
options.D: Private residential homes with no workers present

explanation: Community health nurses reach out to local workplaces like small shops and farms where formal safety officers might not be available. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h8)

question: How do community health nurses bridge the gap between workers and management?

options.A: By advocating for safe practices and helping design workable health policies
options.B: By taking over management duties and running the factory business
options.C: By hiding workplace injuries so the company looks good
options.D: By convincing workers to ignore safety rules to save money

explanation: Nurses act as advocates and educators, helping both sides understand that worker safety benefits everyone. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h8)
